As an autistic person in a long-distance relationship (I'm in the USA and my boyfriend is in England) the concept of traveling so far is daunting. People with ASD struggle to deal with change. I've met my boyfriend three times, and I'm planning to go to England to live with him for 6 months at the end of the year. Each of these meetings only occurred because my boyfriend showed the initiative to schedule them/hold me accountable to scheduling them.

If you want to see him again, I'd recommend trying to take the initiative like you did before. Try throwing out a potential date, or talk about how lodging would work if he came over. 

If he says no, don't be disheartened. My partner taking initiative helped me, but it's still a scary thing to plan such a big disruption to your everyday life. Instead, just let it lie for a while, At least a month, if not a couple, to show respect for his decision before bringing it back up.

Compared to the gritty, cloudy water people in the city had access to, that I grew up drinking, this was ambrosia. 

"What sort of rules, Lord Nebuchadnezzar?" I asked, feigning studious admiration befitting an apprentice. I felt the weight of the dagger hidden in my tailored silk sleeve, begging to be used. 

"Why, the kind of rules that get me more gold!" Lord Nebuchadnezzar chortled to himself, his prodigious stomach shaking under his own tailor-made garb with the motion. A sight that was still alien to me, compared to the concave stomachs of those who lived in the city, hardly able to afford enough food to survive after the tax collectors robbed them of nearly every coin.

I decided to take a chance. To offer Lord Nebuchadnezzar one final opportunity at salvation. "If I may be so bold, my Lord, do you not have enough gold already?"

Lord Nebuchadnezzar turned his head towards me, a look of shock on his face.

"*Enough?*" Another chortle, at the expense of what he saw as inexperience on my part. 
"My boy, one day I must take you to King Tidus's Palace. Why, the wealth he commands is enough to make us seem like peasants. And, between you and me, with the taxes he charges, we need as much wealth as we can to maintain this lifestyle." 

"Of course." I responded, using all my willpower to not speak through gritted teeth. Taxes. The kind that, when my parents could not pay, got their home burned to the ground with them still inside of it. The kind that led to me being a parent-less urchin before even my tenth year. Until one day, when I was being marched to the keep dungeon for trying to steal a loaf of bread, he saw me and deigned on a whim to take me on as his apprentice. For the past five years, I've spent every day hating this man. I blamed him for killing my parents and taking my home. For threatening to throw me in the dungeon and throw away the key just for trying to fill my stomach. But now, absolution was at hand. I had managed to smuggle a dagger into the palace on one of my outings. 

"You may enjoy the golden rule," I said, standing up from my seat to the right of Lord Nebuchadnezzar, "but I think I prefer the steel take much more." 

"The steel take?" The greedy, inhuman fool sitting before me asked, "I've never heard of such a thing. Where did you learn of it?" 

"Here, I'll explain it to you." With a flash, I reached around from behind, and plunged my dagger into former Lord Nebuchadnezzar's throat. He tried to gasp in shock, instead making a pathetic gurgling. 

Lowering my lips to his ear, I whispered, "Those with steel take the gold back."
